environment: Windows 11 Pro x64, MSVC 19.51, GNS 1.6.1 and OpenSSL 3.6.5 via vcpkg 65a2c23, loopback, one process, real time, 1 ms loop
game_exe_sha256: N/A (prototype does not touch the game)
objective: KI-35, review #31 (FB-31-01/02): do intermediate DTLS back-off caps keep EXP-044's tail gain, and at what cost in bytes, resent datagrams and on a path whose RTT exceeds the 250 ms initial timer? Arms on host and client: off (250/500/1000 ms, today's default), cap750 (250/500/750) and cap500 (250/500/500). No default change.
hypothesis: Predeclared (489cacb, before any tooling or run), per backend, each candidate against off: O1 P(total > 3 s) with a 95% Newcombe hybrid score interval; O2 p95/p99 of total by seeded bootstrap (43, 4000); O3 p50 of total and of the DTLS phase on both profiles (reported); G1 mean bytes sent per reconnect (both sides) c/off <= 1.25 on unrounded sums, both profiles; G2 timeouts, failures and reconnects that never started, each with c <= off, both profiles; G3 on the slow profile, p95 and p50 of total not worse. Reading per candidate: 'improves the tail' only if O1 or O2-p95 shows c better on a backend, no 'worse' on any backend for O1, O2-p95 or O2-p99, and G1-G3 hold; otherwise 'not shown'; 'unassessable' or 'incomplete' as predeclared. Intervals 95% per comparison, unadjusted.
procedure: Tooling on 7fcb88c (FB-31-02): DTLS trace details of handshake datagrams end with len=<size> and, for a plaintext handshake message, seq=<message_seq> (header fields only; a new test on both backends, red-before checked). tools/ki35/reconnect_probe.cpp gained arms cap750/cap500, profile slow (150 + U[0,50] ms, 1% loss, no duplicates; RTT 300-400 ms) and per-side bytes sent/received and resent datagrams until each side authenticated; tools/ki35/run_cap_probe.py applies the predeclared rules (9 self-tests). Codex approved the tooling on its first pass. 24 batches of 100 cycles: harsh (15% loss, 5% duplicates, 80 + U[0,40] ms) UDP seeds 4701-4703 and GNS repetitions 1-3 in rotating arm order, slow UDP seed 4704 and GNS repetition 4. Run on 7fcb88c (clean) from 00:53 to about 06:25. Two earlier attempts on the same commit stopped before the end and are kept unjudged: ki35-caps-2026-10-27-103108-7fcb88c (3 complete batches and 38 cycles of udp-4702-cap750-harsh; the runner was a child of the agent session and ended with it) and ki35-caps-2026-10-27-123625-7fcb88c (17 complete batches and 52 cycles of gns-3-cap750-harsh; the runner ended at 16:37:59 with no error output; a Windows Restart Manager session began 34 s earlier; cause not established).
expected_result: If a candidate improves the tail within the guards, choosing it and then a soak gate run is an owner decision; if neither does, neither cap's benefit is demonstrated, and whether EXP-044's gain needs the flat 250 ms timer stays unresolved (this experiment does not compare flat).
observed_result: Complete (24/24 batches, exit 0): 1800 harsh and 600 slow reconnects, 0 timeouts, 0 failures, 0 reconnects that never started; homogeneity held (p >= 0.207); --analyze reproduces verdict.json identically. O1 P(total > 3 s): UDP off 19/300, cap750 25/300 [-0.023, +0.063], cap500 15/300 [-0.052, +0.025]; GNS off 92/300, cap750 82/300 [-0.105, +0.039], cap500 96/300 [-0.061, +0.087]: no difference shown in any comparison. O2 total p95/p99 (ms): UDP off 3153/4398, cap750 3344/4851 (p95 +191 [-409, +586], p99 +453 [-2474, +2656]), cap500 3142/3614 (-11 [-760, +516], -784 [-3680, +1180]); GNS off 4463/6516, cap750 4716/5950 (+253 [-228, +803], -566 [-1465, +1719]), cap500 4535/5785 (+72 [-521, +661], -732 [-1540, +1086]): no difference shown. DTLS phase p99 (reported): UDP 3715 / 4475 / 3239 ms, GNS 4694 / 3014 / 2735 (off / cap750 / cap500). O3 p50 total, harsh: cap750 UDP -1 [-191, +185], GNS -54 [-231, +89]; cap500 UDP +23 [-179, +199], GNS +110 [-166, +224]; slow: cap750 UDP +364 [-53, +415], GNS +1 [-19, +32]; cap500 UDP +27 [-359, +379], GNS +5 [-20, +30]. Guards: G1 bytes ratio cap750 1.016 / 1.000 / 1.013 / 1.001 and cap500 1.003 / 1.003 / 1.000 / 0.999 (UDP harsh, UDP slow, GNS harsh, GNS slow); G2 0 events in every category and arm; G3 slow p95 and p50 no difference shown. Bytes sent per reconnect (both sides): harsh about 2510-2550, slow about 3445-3470 in every arm. Slow profile: about 3.9-4.0 timer fires and 3.0 resent datagrams per side per reconnect in every arm, against 1.7-1.9 and 1.3-1.7 under harsh. Reading by the predeclared rule: cap750 NOT SHOWN, cap500 NOT SHOWN.
errors: The experiment ran as predeclared; only the third attempt is judged. Neither cap is shown to differ from off, in either direction, on any predeclared outcome; the intervals allow meaningful benefits as well as harm. The result does not show that the caps keep EXP-044's tail gain, nor that they cost anything beyond the guard: both passed G1, with observed mean-byte ratios of at most 1.016 (cap750 +1.6% UDP harsh, +1.3% GNS harsh). The DTLS-phase p99 falls with both caps on GNS (reported only, not a rule). On the slow path the timers fire about 4 times per reconnect and each side resends about 3 datagrams, similarly in all three arms. A hypothesis consistent with this, not established here: the 250 ms initial timer, which no arm changed, expires before a 300-400 ms answer. The resend count also includes replies to peer retransmissions and connection restarts, so this comparison does not isolate the cause. One process, loopback, simulated impairment; GNS loss is not seedable. KI-35 is not fixed.
follow_up: No default change. Neither milder cap's benefit is demonstrated by this run; of the settings tested so far only the flat 250 ms timer showed EXP-044's gain, and it stays a bounding arm (RFC 6347 4.2.4.1). Whether the gain needs it stays unresolved. Options for the owner: leave the back-off as is and move KI-35 to the cookie round trip (FB-28-04) or the GNS establishment and session phases (EXP-041), or predeclare a separate study of the initial timer against the path RTT. Any adoption is an owner decision followed by the soak gate.
